Assignment Solvers

Source: R/lap_registry.R
lap_solvers.Rd

lap_solvers() lists the solvers assignment() accepts as method, and register_lap_solver() adds one.

Usage

lap_solvers()

register_lap_solver(
  name,
  solve,
  algorithm = name,
  potentials = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

name

Name under which the solver is selected with assignment(method = name).

solve

The solver function, see Details.

algorithm

Short description shown by lap_solvers().

potentials

Logical; whether solve returns optimal dual potentials u and v of the matrix it receives.

overwrite

Logical; whether to replace an existing solver of the same name. Built-in solvers cannot be replaced.

Value

lap_solvers() returns a tibble with one row per solver and columns method, algorithm, reference, potentials (returns optimal dual potentials), lazy (available with memory_mode = "lazy") and builtin. register_lap_solver() returns name invisibly.

Details

A solver is a function solve(cost, maximize, ...) that receives a numeric matrix with no more rows than columns (forbidden pairs are Inf, or -Inf when maximize = TRUE) and returns either an integer vector giving the column assigned to each row, 0 for an unmatched row, or a list with that vector as match and optionally total_cost, status and the dual potentials u (rows) and v (columns). assignment() transposes wider problems before calling it, computes the status and, for a solver registered here, attaches a certificate by default: verify_assignment() checks the returned potentials when potentials = TRUE and otherwise computes optimal ones, so a registered solver's answer is proved optimal or reported as not.

Examples

lap_solvers()

# A greedy heuristic: each row in turn takes its cheapest free column.
greedy <- function(cost, maximize, ...) {
  if (maximize) cost <- -cost
  match <- integer(nrow(cost))
  free <- rep(TRUE, ncol(cost))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cost))) {
    j <- which(free)[which.min(cost[i, free])]
    match[i] <- j
    free[j] <- FALSE
  }
  match
}
register_lap_solver("greedy_rows", greedy, algorithm = "Row-wise greedy")
cost <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 6, 3, 6, 10), 3)
res <- assignment(cost, method = "greedy_rows")
certificate(res)
